Components

The case for change: what Engineers Australia has learned in transformation

National member event series

Hear directly from Engineers Australia’s leadership as we share what we’ve learned, why change is underway and what it means for you.

About this event series 

Engineers Australia is evolving how we connect with and support our members. 

Through the Horizons strategy and our Member and Customer Experience (MCX) program, we’re modernising systems, services and ways of working. The goal is simple: a more connected, streamlined and valuable experience for you. 

The case for change: what Engineers Australia has learned in transformation is a national event series designed to keep you informed and involved. You’ll hear from our leadership on why this transformation matters, the progress so far and what’s coming next. 

National President and Board Chair Tom Goerke will outline the Board’s vision and strategic direction. Group Executive, Member and Customer Ricky Peña will share practical updates, including improvements to digital services, communication and member engagement. 

Each session includes time for questions and open discussion. 

Who should attend

This series is open to members and non-members across all career stages.

It will be especially valuable if you:

  • volunteer or hold an Office Bearer role
  • want to better understand Engineers Australia’s direction
  • are interested in how changes will improve the member experience.

What you’ll learn

By attending, you will:

  • understand why Engineers Australia is transforming
  • learn key insights and progress from the Horizons strategy
  • see how improvements to systems, services and processes will benefit you
  • gain clarity on what’s next and how to stay informed and involved.

The case for change will be delivered across Australia.

Speakers

Keynote speakers

Kathryn Laurentis
Graduate Researcher – Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, University of Melbourne

Kathryn Laurentis is a chemical engineer, mathematician, and researcher at the University of Melbourne, where she examines the history of Australia's earliest women engineers. A Fellow of Engineers Australia and Chartered Professional Engineer, Kathryn has worked across the energy, resources and government sectors for more than twenty-five years. 

Her research combines engineering and history to recover the stories of Australia's first women engineers, broadening our understanding of the profession's history and heritage. She is passionate about bringing engineering history to wider audiences through public speaking, writing and community engagement.

Professor Miles Lewis AM
Architectural historian and Emeritus Professor – Faculty of Architecture, Building and Planning, University of Melbourne

Miles Lewis AM is an architectural historian and Emeritus Professor at the University of Melbourne. A leading authority on Australian built heritage, he has authored numerous influential books, including Two Hundred Years of Concrete in Australia and Architectura (published in six languages), and has contributed widely to research on architectural history, conservation and urban policy. He is currently working on a book, The Global Building Trade, dealing with international prefabrication in the nineteenth century. 

His work has earned major national awards, and he was appointed a Member of the Order of Australia in 2002 for services to architectural history, heritage protection and urban planning.

Distinguished Professor Mark Stewart
Director – Centre for Built Infrastructure Resilience, University of Technology Sydney

Mark Stewart is a Distinguished Professor of Civil Engineering and Director of the Centre for Built Infrastructure Resilience at the University of Technology Sydney. He is an international leader in risk assessment, public policy decision making, and protective infrastructure for extreme hazards.

He has applied risk assessment and probabilistic methods to a wide range of infrastructure/engineering systems, including terrorism and climate change. His ideas have been presented in four seminal books and many scientific and engineering papers, and has brought engineering and scientific expertise into the public policy domain. 

He is a Fellow of the Australian Academy of Technological Sciences and Engineering, and President of the International Association of Protective Structures.

Under the theme Taking a holistic approach to engineering heritage – past, present and future, the conference explores innovative approaches to heritage investigations, adaptive reuse, sustainable conservation, asset management and the preservation of our shared engineering legacy.

Speakers
Professor Stephen Foster FIEAust
Professor of Structural Engineering, UNSW Sydney

Stephen is a Professor of Structural Engineering at UNSW Sydney and the former Dean of Engineering. He is a Fellow of the Australian Academy of Technological Sciences and Engineering, Fellow of Engineers Australia, Fellow of fib and Honorary Member of the Concrete Institute of Australia. 

Stephen is a member of many Australian and international standards committees for the design of Reinforced and Prestressed Concrete Structures.

John Hilton FIEAust CPEng EngExec NER
Design Director, Bridges and Capability Leader, Aurecon

John is Design Director Bridges at Aurecon. John has more than 50 years’ experience in bridge design and construction within Australia, the Middle East, Southeast Asia, New Zealand and Africa. John is also Adjunct Professor, School of Civil and Environmental Engineering, UNSW.  

In 2018 John was named by Engineers Australia as one of Australia’s 30 most innovative engineers. In his career John has received a number of awards including the 2016 Ray Fisher Technical Excellence Award from Roads Australia and the 2018 John Connell Gold Medal from Engineers Australia.  

John is chair of the Standards Australia AS 5100 Bridge Design committee and a Board member of the Civil College Board, Engineers Australia.

Natasha Stojanovich
Principal Lawyer, Meridian Lawyers

Natasha Stojanovich is a Principal and National Co-Practice Group Leader of Meridian Lawyers’ Professional and Financial Risks team. With more than 15 years’ experience, Natasha acts for construction professionals, including engineers, in the defence of professional indemnity claims. She has a particular interest in the use of artificial intelligence in professional services and support professionals to realise its benefits, while appropriately managing the associated legal risks.

Clare Tubolets
Chief Executive Officer, SmartCrete CRC

Clare is CEO of SmartCrete Cooperative Research Centre, an organisation designed to support the Australian concrete sector to undertake research and development to facilitate decarbonisation. After training as a microbiologist, Clare has had a diverse career in research and government program management spanning various sectors including IoT, Agriculture and now concrete. She is an agile practitioner, passionate about unlocking collaborative innovation potential by bringing together world leading research and industry specialists to solve real-world problems.

Brian Uy FIEAust CPEng NER
Scientia Professor – School of Civil and Environmental Engineering, UNSW

Brian Uy FIStructE CEng is the 2026 President of the Institution of Structural Engineers and Scientia Professor of Structural Engineering in the School of Civil and Environmental Engineering at the University of New South Wales, Sydney, Australia. He currently Chairs the Australian/New Zealand Standards on Steel and Composite Structures for Buildings and Bridges, BD-032 and BD-090-06 and he is a Vice President of the International Association of Bridge and Structural Engineering. 

Brian is an elected Fellow of the Australian Academy of Technological Sciences and Engineering, Engineers Australia, Institution of Structural Engineers, Institution of Civil Engineers, American Society of Civil Engineers, Structural Engineering Institute and the International Association of Bridge and Structural Engineers.

•    Registration and supervision
•    Structural efficiency and embodied carbon
•    Technical competency and research

Structural Engineering and Australian Research Council

Professor Jun Li is a Professor in structural engineering, an Australian Research Council (ARC) mid-career Industry Fellow at Curtin University and Deputy Director of the Centre for Infrastructure Monitoring and Protection. His research focuses on infrastructure intelligence, integrating computer vision, artificial intelligence, IoT sensing and digital twin technologies for structural health monitoring and resilient infrastructure systems. Jun Li has given various presentations which highlight recent advances in AI-driven monitoring, vision-based displacement measurement, digital twin integration, and real-world deployment of these technologies on operational infrastructure. His work has been closely conducted with industry partners such as Main Roads WA, with outcomes contributing to national guidelines and field applications.

Recent developments in concrete design standards in Australia

Professor Stephen Foster, a member of several Australian and international standards committees for the design of reinforced and prestressed concrete structures, will facilitate a dedicated series of presentations at ASEC 2026 exploring recent developments in concrete design standards in Australia.

Topics will include:
•    Assessment and design of existing concrete structures in accordance with AS 3600
•    Practical implications of recent changes to the seismic design provisions in AS 3600 and AS 1170.4
•    Developments in punching shear design in AS 3600:2026
•    Material models and design properties for UHPC bridge structures in AS 5100 Part 10
•    Durability provisions for UHPC bridge structures in AS 5100 Part 10

This session series will provide practical insights into the latest standards updates and their implications for structural engineering design and practice.

Karol Miller
Winthrop Professor, The University of Western Australia

Abstract Title: Applied mechanics meets medicine: success stories from neuro and vascular surgery

Karol Miller is a Winthrop Professor of Applied Mechanics and the Director of Intelligent Systems for Medicine Laboratory at The University of Western Australia. Until 2023 he has been a Visiting Professor of Radiology at Harvard Medical School. 

The overall objective of Karol’s research is to help creating methods and tools which will enable a new exciting era of personalised medicine. Karol's research and teaching have been recognised by multiple awards, including the Humboldt Research Award, NVIDIA GPU Computing Champion Award, the Simulation Industry Association Australia Award, the Sir Charles Julius Medal, and the UWA Student Guild Choice Award.

Elena Pasternak
Professor, The University of Western Australia

Abstract Title: Mechanics of topological interlocking structures

Professor Elena Pasternak received BSc and MSc in Mechanics and Applied Mathematics in 1997 from Dnepropetrovsk State University, Ukraine, and PhD in 2002 from the University of Western Australia. In 2002 she became a Humboldt Fellow at Technical University of Clausthal, Germany. Elena is a Professor at the Department of Mechanical Engineering, School of Engineering of the University of Western Australia. Her research interests include different areas in fracture mechanics, rock mechanics, wave propagation and vibrations, topological interlocking, auxetics and negative stiffness. 

Gwénaëlle Proust PhD, CMatP
Professor, The University of Sydney

Abstract Title: Additive manufacturing: opportunities and challenges

Professor Gwénaëlle Proust is Academic Director of the Sydney Manufacturing Hub at the University of Sydney and a Professor of Materials Engineering. Her work focuses on understanding processing-microstructure–property relationships in materials, with an emphasis on additive manufacturing of metals and alloys. She combines experimental characterisation with modelling approaches to study material behaviour and processing. She has published widely in the field and works closely with industry and academic partners to support research and development in advanced manufacturing. Her role at the Sydney Manufacturing Hub involves enabling research projects and supporting users across a range of manufacturing technologies.

Gangadhara Prusty FRSN FIEAust
Scientia Professor, UNSW Sydney

Abstract Title: Translational research in biomaterials: from innovation to commercialisation

Gangadhara Prusty is a Scientia Professor at UNSW Sydney and Founding Director of the Centre for Automated Manufacture of Advanced Composites (AMAC). He has provided national leadership in advanced manufacturing, playing a central role in the conception, establishment and delivery of the $250M Advanced Composites Manufacturing Cooperative Research Centre (ACM CRC), a flagship initiative transforming Australia’s composites capability and industry competitiveness. He has authored over 300 peer-reviewed publications, supervised 38 higher degree researchers and delivered impactful innovations, including patented dental composites. He is internationally recognised for contributions to adaptive e-learning and engineering education, receiving multiple national awards for excellence in university teaching.

Fang-Bao Tian
Associate Professor, School of Engineering and Technology, University of New South Wales

Abstract Title: Bio-inspired flapping wings: from natural flyers to MAVs on Mars

A/Prof Fang-Bao Tian is an Associate Professor in the School of Engineering and Technology, UNSW, Canberra. He started his career at UNSW as an RA in 2013. He was appointed as a Lecturer in 2014, and promoted to Senior Lecturer in 2017 and to Associate Professor in 2022. His research interest covers computational fluid dynamics methods and applications in fluid-structure-interaction problems and complex flows. He is the recipient of ARC DECRA 2016 and Lead CI of two ARC DPs. He also leads many industry, government and defence projects. He has been actively devoting himself in many professional services.

Hao Wang
Distinguished Professor, Swinburne University of Technology

Abstract Title: New and future developments of carbon fibre composites

Hao Wang is the Distinguished Professor of Composite Materials at Swinburne University of Technology. Previously he was the Professor of Materials and Manufacturing at University of Southern Queensland and was the Director of the Centre for Future Materials there. He was the President of the Asian Association for Composite Materials.

Professor Wang has over 30 years of research experience on carbon fibre composites, plastic recycling and green concrete. He has published over 500 journal papers, with Google Scholar h-index of 115 and over 55,00 citations. He is a Clarivate Highly Cited Researcher.

Professor Wang is currently the Editor-in-Chief of Safety Science and Technology. Previously he was the Editor-in-Chief of Composites Part B, the top journal in composite materials research, where he brought the journal’s Impact Factor from 4.9 to 14.2.

Speakers

Discover the esteemed line-up of expert speakers who presented at Transport 2026.

 

Chris Blackstock
Senior Associate Geospatial Consultant, Jacobs

Chris is a recognised geospatial and strategic leader with 25 years’ experience developing, delivering and leading impactful geospatial and digital programs, infrastructures, innovations, and value across the public, private and government sectors in both Australia and North America.   


He has proven experience building and leading technical teams and programs focused on addressing critical community and industry challenges through the delivery of digital and geospatial systems, services, technology and programs.


This has included multiple innovative and transformational state and national level transport and government programs in Australia and internationally, where Digital Twins, AI, semantic models and other emerging technologies have delivered game-changing results and value. 

Miranda Blogg
Acting Executive Director (Transport Operational Technology), Engineering and Technology Branch, Infrastructure Management and Delivery, Queensland Department of Transport and Main Roads

Dr Miranda Blogg is the Director of Safer Roads at the Queensland Department of Transport and Main Roads. She oversees the targeted road safety program development and delivery in partnership with state and local jurisdictions. In 2025, she received the ITS Australia Woman of the Year award, recognising contributions to intelligent transport systems and road safety. Dr Blogg has over 25 years of experience as a civil engineer in both private and public sectors, specialising in transport planning, delivery, operations and research. 

Natalya Boujenko
Strategic Consultant & Director, Intermethod

Natalya Boujenko is a founding Director at Intermethod, with professional and academic experience spanning Australia and the UK. She co-authored Link and Place: A Guide to Street Planning and Design, which helped introduce the Movement and Place approach to international practice. More recently, she led the development of South Australia’s Active Travel Design Guide and Healthy Active by Design.
Natalya brings deep expertise in integrated transport planning, infrastructure, street design and community engagement. She is driven by a strong belief that well-designed streets and neighbourhoods can directly improve everyday health, liveability and long-term sustainability. She is passionate about translating good policy into meaningful outcomes on the ground.

Bridget Doran
Transport Engineer and Researcher, Bridget Doran Consulting

Bridget is a transport engineer and researcher from Hamilton, New Zealand. She works on a planning, policy and research projects for public and private sector clients. Bridget grounds her work in an appreciation of the biophysical limits of the earth. Her practice focuses on inclusion of, and compassion for the human at the heart of transport investment decisions. Most of her work is in road safety and accessibility. Bridget has degrees in civil and transportation engineering and a doctorate in applied cognitive psychology. She is a Chartered Member of Engineering New Zealand.

Anthony Dunn
Chief Technical Principal (Rail), SMEC

Tony is a passionate Chartered Engineer (EA) who is currently Chief Technical Principal for SMEC’s Global Rail & Metro Business. He utilises over 28 years’ of industry experience to provide subject matter expert information / coordination for a variety of future shaping projects across the globe and is an active member of Engineers Australia (including RTSA) and has been Treasurer for Permanent Way Institute Qld Branch (PWI) for 16 years.

Tony started in the UK as a track engineer with a pencil, rule and drawing board until computer aided design software’s started to be implemented in the late 90’s and undertook site surveys, design, manufacturing inspections through to construction setout / supervision.

He has led and worked on global major multidiscipline rail projects and has been influential in the strategic planning of initial concepts through to the delivery of major Australian projects over the last 20 years.

Tony is currently the Design Manager (SMEC/WSP Design Joint Venture) for the Beerburrum to Nambour rail upgrade project in the Sunshine Coast working closely with DTMR, QR and the constructors, SWC & JHG. Leading the multidiscipline rail corridor and road delivery.

With innovation constantly on the horizon, Tony is passionate about leading discussions for the future of the railway industry, and mentoring generations to focus on emerging technologies with a key reminder to also look back as historic solutions and methods that can also generate innovative ideas with new technology that wasn’t present at the time.

Scott Elaurant
Principal Six Cats Consulting

Scott is a civil engineer/economist with 40 years’ experience in infrastructure planning, design and economics. He worked for Jacobs for 13 years as transport planning lead for their Adelaide office. Prior to joining Jacobs in 2006 Scott was head of discipline for road planning in Queensland Main Roads. 
In recent years Scott has focused on infrastructure planning and business cases. As Six Cats Consulting he offer services in transport planning and economics for roads, active transport, public transport and streetscapes. He is National Chair of the Transport Australia Society.

Madison Elliott
Chartered Civil Engineer, Burchills Engineering Solutions

Madison is a Chartered Civil Engineer at Burchills Engineering Solutions with over 8 years’ experience in the transport industry. Madison’s experience has seen her leading civil infrastructure and active transport planning and design projects throughout Australia for a variety of local government clients. Madison enjoys collaborating within design teams and with clients to ensure there are no assumptions to provide the best fit for purpose solution. 

Her curious nature prompts innovative and creative thinking to provide design solutions that challenge the status quo. Her variety of experience in the traffic and civil infrastructure fields allow her to gain a more holistic understanding of a project to flag opportunities and constraints early to optimise project development.

Clare Gardiner-Barnes
Commissioner, Infrastructure Australia

Clare Gardiner-Barnes is a Commissioner for Infrastructure Australia. With senior leadership roles across New South Wales, Queensland and the Northern Territory, she has helped shape major transport strategies, freight planning and infrastructure investment programs across Australia. Clare previously served as Deputy Secretary for Freight, Strategy and Planning at Transport for NSW and Head of Strategy, Planning and Innovation at Infrastructure NSW, working on major transport and freight initiatives supporting growing cities and regional economies. She is a strong advocate for practical reform and collaboration across the infrastructure sector.

Sara Haider
Civil Infrastructure Lead Specialist, Transport for NSW

Sara Haider is the Civil Infrastructure Lead Specialist at Transport for NSW and a PhD researcher at the Institute of Transport and Logistics Studies at the University of Sydney. She has contributed to major transport projects across NSW, spanning regional roads, metropolitan networks and tunnel infrastructure. Her research explores how transport infrastructure can be designed to respond to human behaviour across diverse contexts, supporting more sustainable and equitable transport systems. 

Sara is passionate about positioning the transport industry at the forefront of innovation and technology, including through contributions to national AI initiatives that seek to make infrastructure more efficient, effective, economical and resilient.

Courtney Hansen
Chief Executive Officer, North Marine

Courtney Hansen is the Managing Director and owner of North Marine, a Cairns-based maritime services provider delivering project and logistics support across Northern Australia. With operations spanning the Great Barrier Reef, Torres Strait and Gulf of Carpentaria, she leads a company known for supporting defence, government, research, tourism and infrastructure projects in remote and complex environments.

Courtney is recognised for her strong leadership, operational expertise and commitment to regional industry development. In 2025, she was named “Woman of the Year” at the Cairns Regional Council International Women’s Day Awards, reflecting her impact on both the maritime sector and the broader community. She is a 2026 Lowy Institute ELD alumi and a passionate advocate for expanding regional capabilities and workforce development.
 

Bill Hanway
Executive Vice President, AECOM

Bill Hanway is an Executive Vice President at AECOM, where he leads the firm’s global Sports and Social Infrastructure practice. A trained architect, Bill specialises in large-scale urban regeneration, major event masterplanning, and the design of world-class sports venues.

He works closely with governments, civic leaders and key stakeholders to leverage major event investments to deliver long-term social and economic benefits, particularly in areas undergoing urban renewal.

Bill currently leads AECOM’s role on the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games. He previously led AECOM’s work on the Rio 2016 Games and Legacy Masterplan, contributed to the London 2012 Games and Legacy programme, and advised the Tokyo Metropolitan Government on the Tokyo 2020 Games.

Beyond global events, Bill is leading the design of the Intuit Dome, the future home of the LA Clippers, a net-zero carbon, LEED Platinum venue. His portfolio also includes the Golden 1 Center in Sacramento, the world’s first LEED Platinum sports arena, and a major campus expansion for the University of Cambridge.

Bill holds a Master of Architecture from the Harvard Graduate School of Design.

Mary Haverland
Founding Director, Avandra Advisory

Mary Haverland is a transport industry leader with 30 years’ experience across Australia, the UK and internationally. With qualifications in urban planning and civil engineering, she brings a multidisciplinary perspective to shaping transport, places and communities. Mary is the Founding Director of Avandra Advisory and a Non Executive Director of the Transport Professionals Association. Proudly living and working in regional Tasmania, she is closely engaged with contemporary policy, governance and market trends, and regularly presents at conferences and industry events on city shaping, future mobility and the role of transport in creating better communities.

Kieron Hendicott
Deputy Chief Executive Officer, Infrastructure Western Australia

Kieron has a proven track record in establishing and leading high-impact teams and organisations that navigate complex community and stakeholder environments to develop and deliver nationally significant projects and achieve corporate goals. Prior to joining Infrastructure WA, Kieron worked in senior executive roles in the NSW Government over the last 10 years. This included leading the delivery of a >$1 billion climate adaption program, as well as strategy, policy and project leadership roles with Infrastructure NSW, Infrastructure WA's counterpart agency. Kieron holds a Bachelor of Engineering degree, as well as a Masters of Commerce from the University of Sydney, and a Masters of Science in Sustainable Urban Development from the University of Oxford.

David Hensher AM
Professor and Founding Director, Institute of Transport and Logistics Studies (ITLS) | The University of Sydney Business School

Professor David A. Hensher AM PhD FASSA is a distinguished transport economist and the Founding Director of the Institute of Transport and Logistics Studies (ITLS) at the University of Sydney. Internationally recognised for pioneering contributions to discrete choice modelling, stated preference methods, economic valuation and travel behaviour analysis, his work has profoundly influenced transport policy and infrastructure planning. 

With over 84,500 citations and 765 publications, Professor Hensher ranks among the most cited economists globally. In 2023, he was appointed a Member of the Order of Australia. Recipient of numerous awards. In 2026, David is ranked #1 globally for scientists in transport and logistics.

Michael Hopkins
Chief Executive Officer and Commissioner, National Transport Commission

Michael is the Chief Executive Officer and Commissioner at the National Transport Commission and has had a long career in transport policy at the State, Territory and national level. With over thirty years experience in policy development he brings significant expertise in transport reform to his role and has worked on major transport reforms during that time.
Michael is passionate about the provision of robust and independent evidence-based advice to Australia’s transport ministers and engaging with our many stakeholders, to improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of Australia’s transport system.
Prior to joining the NTC as CEO, Michael was previously an Executive Leader at the NTC driving the organisation’s strategy and work program, the delivery of reforms and the Commission’s relationship with its partner governments. Prior to that Michael worked as a consultant providing expert advice to industry and national, state and local governments on responding to the contemporary challenges faced by the section.
As a senior executive in Victoria's Department of Transport, Michael delivered future-focused policy reforms, network strategy and planning, as well as stronger governance to improve the way transport works.
Michael has a Masters in public administration from the Australian and New Zealand School of Government and University of Melbourne and a Bachelor of Arts in philosophy.

Luke Host
Project Director, TSA Riley

Luke is a Chartered Civil Engineer and Project Manager with over 16 years’ experience working on a variety of major infrastructure projects in the transport sector, both interstate and overseas. Since joining TSA Riley as a Project Director in mid-2022 Luke has been the key lead on the Kimberley Flood Recovery Works. Previously, Luke delivered outstanding outcomes at Major Road Projects Victoria through his leadership on several major transport projects. Luke also spent two years in the Ecologiq programme, working across the Victorian Big Build to optimise the use of Victorian recyclables in all major transport infrastructure projects. 

Ali Inayathusein
Executive Director (Digital), Veitch Lister Consulting

Ali Inayathusein is Executive Director (Digital) at Veitch Lister Consulting, where he leads the firm’s digital platforms, data products and services, including the Planwisely platform. With over 17 years’ experience across transport modelling, data analytics and evidence based planning, Ali specialises in applying emerging datasets and digital tools to inform strategic infrastructure and policy decisions. 

He has led major analytics initiatives across Australia and New Zealand and previously held senior roles at Transport for London, where he pioneered the use of mobile data in transport modelling. Ali holds an MSc in transport and an Executive MBA.

Darlene Irvine
Chief Executive Officer, FNQ Regional Organisation of Councils (FNQROC)

Darlene is the CEO of FNQROC and her journey began in 2001 with the FNQ2010 (Regional Plan), and she’s been deeply involved in regional planning and collaboration ever since. Known for her practical, down-to-earth approach, she has a knack for turning complex regional challenges into achievable actions.

Reporting to a Board of Mayors, she’s helped deliver countless collaborative projects, studies and strategies that have made a real difference across the region.

Darryl Jones
District Director, Far North, North Queensland Region

Darryl Jones is a visionary and strategic leader with more than 25 years’ experience guiding multi disciplinary teams across government in North Queensland. Renowned for his authoritative and professional approach, he excels in delivering expert advice within dynamic, collaborative environments. Darryl brings high-level proficiency in people leadership, project and program management, and stakeholder engagement, consistently driving initiatives that deliver public value. His proven track record reflects a commitment to aligning outcomes with strategic objectives while fostering strong relationships and high-performance cultures. Darryl’s leadership style is grounded in integrity, innovation and a steadfast dedication to community-focused results.

Steve Kanowski
Director, TransEcon

Steve Kanowski is a transport economist with over 40 years’ experience advising on a range of economic, commercial and policy issues in transport and infrastructure - roads / highways (incl. toll roads) aviation, maritime and railways. Steve has international experience having advised Governments, private investors and multi-lateral lending institutions on major transport infrastructure projects in over 20 countries. 
Prior to joining Deloitte in 2017, Steve was Chief Economist QTMR.  He now operates a boutique consultancy -TransEcon. Prior to joining Government in 2013, Steve had been in consulting with leading Australian and international firms – GHD, Booz & Co, PwC and SKM. 

Kitar Kue
Engineer (Civil), Department of Transport and Main Roads

Kitar has worked across private and public engineering sectors to deliver road infrastructure and planning projects for the Far North District. As a Cairns local, she seeks to work towards a long-term vision for the region, where the region’s transport infrastructure is safe for all road users. She volunteers with Engineers Australia’s Cairns Regional Group and currently is involved as the Cairns Regional Lead in the YEAQ Committee. 

Kitar advocates for equality, diversity and female representation in engineering and seeks to grow the engineering community in Cairns by strengthening the working relationships between young engineers and seasoned, experienced professionals.

Todd Litman
Founder and Executive Director , Victoria Transport Policy Institute

Todd Litman is founder and executive director of the Victoria Transport Policy Institute, an independent research organization dedicated to developing innovative solutions to transport problems. His work helps expand the range of impacts and options considered in transportation decision-making, improve evaluation methods and make specialised technical concepts accessible to a larger audience. 

Nathan Lee Long
Associate Project Manager, Jacobs

Nathan Lee Long is the Jacobs’ Cairns Office Leader and Northern Australia Civil and Aviation Team Lead. 

With his team they are enhancing the regions of Northern Australia through delivery of new communities, municipal infrastructure and transport solutions. Nathan has more than 22 years of experience leading various projects within the region. 

Nathan brings the perspective of regional and remote delivery of projects with an understanding of the end user gained from stakeholder and community engagement and being a proud 6th generation FNQ local. Nathan is also the UDIA Queensland FNQ Branch President representing the development and housing industry in Far North Queensland.

Kate Mackay
Principal, Arup

A Principal at Arup, Kate is the Queensland Transport Planning Business Leader. A geographer by background, Kate’s approach to transport planning has always been focused on creating and shaping better places for people to live, work and play. Recognised for her pragmatic approach to complex challenges, Kate collaborates with clients to help articulate and deliver their vision, acknowledging and unpacking the uncertainties ahead. Through her deep understanding of travel behaviour, she leads the design and implementation of user focused integrated transport strategies, considering spatial, transport and digital access. She has a reputation for using innovative and creative techniques in transport planning, like design thinking, systems thinking and personas. Previously Kate led the Australia Transport Planning Practice for Mott MacDonald, prior to this she ran her own consultancy in Fiji, and she started her career with Steer Davies Gleave (now Steer) in London and South Africa. She has a MSc in Transport from Imperial College/University College London and a BA Hons degree from Newcastle University.

Cameron Messer
Executive Director, Network Operations, Queensland Department of Transport and Main Roads

Cameron Messer is the Executive Director, Network Operations at the Queensland Department of Transport and Main Roads. He leads the coordination and optimisation of Queensland’s road and transport networks, with a focus on real-time operations, incident management and cross-agency collaboration. Cameron plays a key role in shaping the future of integrated transport operations, including the development of the Transport Coordination Centre (TCC) to support major events such as Brisbane 2032. With extensive experience in complex network management, he is passionate about delivering resilient, connected and customer-focused transport outcomes that keep people and freight moving across Queensland.

Peter Milward
General Manager, Olympic & Paralympic Coordination Branch; Policy, Planning and Investment Division, Department of Transport and Main Roads

Peter Milward was appointed General Manager of the Olympic and Paralympic Coordination (OPC) Branch in 2025. He leads the Department of Transport and Main Roads’ preparations for the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games, overseeing strategic planning, governance and integration across the Games Transport Program to ensure alignment with state-wide priorities and stakeholder expectations. With over 35 years of experience across public and private sectors, Peter brings extensive expertise to ensure Queensland’s transport network will be ready for the Games while delivering lasting benefits for the community.

Colin Mitchell
National General Manager, Strategy, BMD

Colin has more than 30 years of operational and technical experience across a range of mining, port, defence, road and rail projects. As National General Manager (Strategy), Colin leads the company’s strategic planning process with the explicit objective of achieving sustainable growth across the BMD business units through diversification and competitive advantage. 

Prior to his role as National General Manager (Strategy), Colin was the long serving Regional Manager for North Queensland. During his time in this role, Colin successfully led the business through the challenges of the Global Financial Crisis and subsequent rapid growth phase producing record turnovers and safety milestones and affirming BMD as a market leader in the region. Colin was also President of Engineers Australia in 2020, reflecting his leadership and expertise in the industry and making him a highly fitting speaker for the Engineers Australia Transport Conference.
 

Betty Moinet
Senior Manager, Strategic Engagement, Esri Australia

Betty Moinet is Senior Manager, Strategic Engagement at Esri Australia. She works with executive leaders across government and industry to translate geospatial capability into clear, trusted insight that supports confident decision making. 

With a background in leadership, planning and stakeholder engagement, Betty is known for connecting people, priorities and place to help organisations navigate complexity and achieve real world outcomes. Her experience includes defining the geospatial strategy for the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games and founding the South East Queensland GIS Managers Community of Practice. 

Today, she focuses on building influential networks across Asia Pacific to advance the role of location intelligence in leadership and long term strategy. 

Graham Nelmes
General Manager Customer, Place and Operations, High Speed Rail Authority

Graham is responsible for shaping the future customer experience, operational strategies, maintenance planning, and integrated transport and place outcomes for Australia’s east coast high-speed rail network. 
Graham has more than 20 years’ experience in the planning, development and delivery of major rail projects across NSW, including Sydney Metro. He has played lead roles in delivering city-shaping and state-shaping projects and developed several major cross-government initiatives, including with the Australian and ACT governments.

Michael Nieuwesteeg
Director, Road Safety & Design Program, Austroads

Michael leads Austroads’ Road Safety & Design program, managing a portfolio of guidance, research and implementation projects. With a background in data and statistics, he has worked in road safety since 2008, developing and delivering research and evaluation programs and overseeing investments in infrastructure safety upgrades and community road safety initiatives.

Matthew Raisbeck
Principal Adviser (Transport), Infrastructure Victoria

Matthew is Principal Adviser, Transport at Infrastructure Victoria where he develops, leads and delivers large-scale infrastructure planning and policy advice on the state’s long-term needs. He recently led the transport and land use integration recommendations within the Victoria's 30-year Infrastructure Strategy.

With more than 20 years’ experience in the transport industry across government and the private sector, he has worked in roles across data analytics, modelling, policy, business cases, economics and planning. He uses best practice research and building partnerships with stakeholders to develop solutions for the cities and regions of Victoria
 

Shalendra Ram
National Executive Committee Immediate Past Chair, Transport Australia Society

Shalendra Ram is a senior engineering executive with extensive experience across public and private sectors, specialising in transport strategy, project leadership and client engagement. A recognised industry leader and former National Chair of Engineers Australia’s Transport Australia Society, he is known for driving innovation, inclusive leadership and shaping integrated transport and land use outcomes across Australia.

Emmerson Richardson
Deputy Chair WA, Transport Australia Society

Emmerson has over 40 years’ experience in transport policy, strategic planning and transport system development and management. A consistent theme has been his support for, integrated, multi-modal transport systems that are adaptable, affordable and easy and safe to use by all, including cyclists and walkers. 

He played an important role in gaining approval for the rail tunnel under Perth CBD linking the Northern and Southern railways. More recently, he has assisted Transport Australia Society to advocate for a systems approach in urban transport planning and transition to safer and more liveable urban streets, through low cost, high value implementation works.

Sara Stace
Director, Vivendi Consulting

Sara Stace is a registered architect with a 30-year career spanning transport, urban design, planning and infrastructure delivery across federal, state and local government. She has held senior leadership roles including Director of Cities at WSP and is now a Director at Vivendi Consulting. Sara is recognised as a WSP Technical Excellence Fellow, the firm’s highest global acknowledgement of technical expertise and leadership. Her work focuses on integrated, evidence-based land use and transport planning to deliver lower emissions, better places and long-term infrastructure value.

Emilie van de Graaff
Director, Operations and Performance, MR5, Department of Transport and Planning, Victoria

Emilie is an executive leader with long experience of leading and managing people. She has worked across the spectrum of transport and infrastructure with experience in both public and private sectors and has worked in both policy and operational roles.

Emilie is the chair of the Women in Transport committee which is part of Transport Australia Society. A graduate of the Australian Institute of Company Directors, she is on the board of The Fair Co, an organisation that supports companies in diversity, equality and inclusion, and social procurement work. She is a mentor on a number of national and state based mentoring programs.

Emilie is currently the Director for Operations and Performance for the Metropolitan Rail Refranchising project at the Department of Transport and Planning in Victoria. She also undertakes some consultancy work. Emilie founded her own business, Elleeva Associates, in August 2020 and has been involved in a range of projects nationally that range from policy, strategy and contract development, bid preparation, and gateway reviews for high value, high risk projects.

Emilie’s has a strong interest in what makes towns and cities thrive, with a focus on social inclusion and the environment, and that’s what drives her dedication to create an effective transport network to support people living their daily lives.

Trent Williams
Business Leader, Transport QLD, Stantec

Trent is passionate about creating people-focused transport solutions and solving complex challenges through collaboration. As Stantec’s Business Leader for Transport in Queensland, he leads a team of talented planners, modellers, engineers and designers who are committed to making a meaningful difference in the communities which they live, work, play and travel. Together, this team is supporting the planning, design and delivery of state significant precincts and crucial future transport infrastructure projects right across Queensland.

Nikhil Yadav
Master’s engineering student, RMIT University Melbourne

Nikhil Yadav is a Master’s engineering student at RMIT University, Melbourne, specialising in transport and infrastructure systems. He has developed technical experience using industry-relevant software, including OpenRail Designer, and is currently undertaking a transport research thesis focused on real-world engineering challenges. Alongside his academic work, Nikhil serves as a student ambassador, where he builds strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills. He is passionate about sustainable transport solutions and aims to contribute to the development of efficient and resilient infrastructure systems.

George Yannis
Professor, National Technical University of Athens

George Yannis is Professor in Traffic and Safety Engineering with particular focus on Data Science and Director of Traffic Engineering Laboratory of the School of Civil Engineering at the National Technical University of Athens (NTUA). For more than 30 years, he has contributed extensively in more than 350 research and engineering projects and studies and in several scientific committees of the European Commission and other International Organisations (UNECE, OECD, WHO, World Bank, EIB, CEDR, ERF, IRF, PIARC, UITP, ETSC, ECTRI, WCTR, TRB). He has published more than 1000 scientific papers (284 in scientific journals) widely cited worldwide.

22 May 2025
Gala dinner

The RISK Gala dinner provides a unique opportunity to forge lasting relationships, share insights and reflect on the innovative ideas presented.

Enjoy a meal in a distinguished setting while engaging in meaningful conversations with peers and industry leaders. 

Site visits and workshops

Elevate your RISK 2025 experience by adding a site tour to your existing registration. With limited spaces available, secure your spot today.

Pre-conference workshop

Members could claim CPD hours for attending this workshop: 6 hours 45 minutes

  Wednesday 21 May
Pre-conference workshop
Registration: 8.00 am AEST
Workshop: 8.30am – 5.00pm AEST
Engineers Australia Melbourne office
Key solutions for quantitative cost and schedule risk analysis

Supported by experts from six leading QRA solutions in the engineering and construction sectors, this full-day workshop is designed to provide you with essential methodologies and tools for quantitative risk analysis of project costs and schedules. 

You'll also receive the newly released 3rd edition of the RES Contingency Guideline, along with a brief presentation on its contents.

Learning outcomes

By the end of this workshop, you'll be able to:

  • Understand the fundamentals of QRA modelling and visualisations with different QRA solutions for risk management in the engineering industry– noting that there will be 6 concurrent sessions for different solutions.
  • Have opportunities to share knowledge, experience and tips with peers and other participants  
  • Understand the principles and importance of quantitative risk analysis in project management.
  • Learn to identify and quantify risks related to project costs and schedules.
  • Gain proficiency in using QRA tools and techniques such as Monte Carlo simulation and probabilistic risk assessment.
  • Apply quantitative risk analysis methods to real-world scenarios through practical exercises and case studies.
  • Enhance decision-making capabilities by integrating risk analysis into project planning and execution. 
Pricing
  • Member: $300
  • Non-member: $400
  • Student: $150

*Workshop registration is at an additional cost to full or day conference registration.

  Wednesday 21 May
Site visit and workshop at Swinburne University of Technology
Registration: 9.00 am AEST
Workshop: 9.30 – 11.00 am AEST
Tour of facilities: 11.30 am – 12:30 pm
EN615, Engineering Building, Swinburne University of Technology, John St, Hawthorn VIC 3122
Simulation modelling and visualisations for risk management in engineering projects

Register to join us for an immersive workshop designed to equip engineering professionals with cutting-edge tools and techniques for effective risk management in industry projects and infrastructure assets. Gain foundational insights into specialised simulation and visualisation methods tailored for engineering challenges. 

The tour of facilities will include:

  • Factory of Future
  • Smart Structures Lab
  • Digital Construction Lab
  • Trimble Technology Lab
  • Construction Simulation Hub
Learning outcomes

By the end of this workshop, you'll be able to: 

  • Understand the fundamentals of simulation modelling and visualisations with digital technologies for risk management in the engineering industry. 
  • Recognise potential use of building information modelling, virtual reality, mixed reality and holographic applications for identifying and mitigating risks in engineering projects and infrastructure asset management. 
  • Value utilising simulation models and visualisation tools to interpret and communicate risk data effectively. 
Pricing
  • Member: $80
  • Non-member: $90
  • Student: $40

*Site visit registration will include access to:
1. Site visit and workshop at Swinburne University of Technology
2. Site visit at Master Builders Victoria 

  Wednesday 21 May
Site visit at Master Builders Victoria
Wednesday 21 May
3.00pm – 6.00pm AEST
Master Builders Victoria, Leadership Simulation Centre

A tour and taster session will be held at the Leadership Simulation Centre at Master Builders Victoria, featuring a mini expo of industry suppliers. 

Unlike traditional training, the controlled simulation environment enhances learning by allowing participants to apply skills immediately, improving retention while reducing real-world risks like injury and costs. 

Participants can practice and refine new skills in a safe setting, receiving expert feedback and reflection from skilled observers. Our courses combine classroom learning, feedback workshops and simulated site experiences, enabling participants to take on leadership roles and apply their knowledge effectively.

The session will focus on conflict resolution, allowing participants to observe various interactions in our site sheds. These demonstrations will showcase how individuals being challenged with a variety of tasks, interactions and real-site scenarios can navigate towards effective solutions.

Learning outcomes

By the end of this session, you'll be able to:

  • Understand a different, more immersive way of training with applications in behavioural, technical and leadership learning.
  • Recognise the potential use of simulation learning as it immerses your team in the challenges of a real building site without the risk of injuries, cost blow outs and delays or defects. This in turn ensures your projects are safer, quicker and more cost effective.
  • Value utilising simulation training to interpret and communicate risk data effectively. 
Pricing
  • Member: $80
  • Non-member: $90
  • Student: $40

*Site visit registration will include access to:
1. Site visit and workshop at Swinburne University of Technology
2. Site visit at Master Builders Victoria 

Speakers

RISK 2025 showcased an exciting line-up of expert speakers. 

Keynote speakers

Andrew Gissing
CEO, Natural Hazards Research

Andrew is the CEO of Natural Hazards Research Australia. He works with government, business and not-for-profits to make our communities safer and more resilient.

Andrew has more than 20 years disaster management experience, including in senior executive roles. He previously held the position of Deputy Chief Officer / Director Emergency Management and Communication with the Victoria State Emergency Service and, before joining Natural Hazards Research Australia was a General Manager at Risk Frontiers.

Andrew holds Masters (Hons) of Science and Bachelor of Economics degrees and has published in leading international journals.

Presentation: Be ahead of ready: tackling challenges and harnessing opportunities in the face of natural hazards
Jessica Ottner
General Manager Internal Audit, APA Group

Jessica is a seasoned chief audit executive with extensive global experience leading internal audit, risk management and governance functions across industries, including infrastructure, utilities and gas. 

Currently the General Manager of Internal Audit at APA Group, Jessica has worked with executives, boards and regulators worldwide, including presenting at Royal Commissions. 

Jessica is passionate about the role of risk and assurance in supporting the achievement of strategic objectives and navigating change.

Assuring tomorrow: Evolving assurance to navigate the complexities of infrastructure projects in the energy transition
Sirish Parekh
Head of Estimating and Benchmarking, UK Government, Infrastructure & Projects Authority

Sirish is Head of Estimating and Benchmarking at the Infrastructure and Project Authority in UK Government. Previous to this he was at National Highways as a Commercial Intelligence Manager and Estimating Manager, with experience in cost estimating & modelling, risk and uncertainty management and project controls. He has held various positions in Rolls-Royce as a Programme Manager on implementing Single Source Contract Regulations (SSCR), an Estimating Specialist, Supportability Engineering Manager and Whole Life Cost Engineer. He is currently developing intelligence reporting using historical data and introducing a career learning journey for the estimating profession.

Sirish Co-Chairs PsACE (Public Sector Advisory Community for Estimating), a group with 40 UK government departments and arms length bodies and development of a new Estimating British Standard.

Using his current role, experience and network, Sirish aspires to introduce consistency in estimates across government projects and improved benchmarking to achieve better value for money and project outcomes.

Mike Robertson
Head of Portfolio Management Excellence, NEOM

Mike spent eight years in Saudi Arabia, two years as Head of Project Risk for NEOM, one year as Head of Portfolio Management and Governance Excellence, two years with Khatib and Alami and three with Bechtel as Director of Professional Excellence on KSA major projects. 

Mike also spent 17 years as the Managing Director of Risk Solutions, a UK-based consultancy, where he led all the transport and infrastructure sector work, and has 15 years in the nuclear industry.

Mike was a non-executive director of the UK Major Projects Association for more than 10 years. He was a founding member of the North West and Kingdoms of Saudi Arabia and Bahrain regional groups of the Institute of Risk Management.

Presentation: There and back again: a journey through 40 years of risk management
Ben Ryan
Executive Project Director, Metro Tunnel Project

Ben Ryan is the Executive Project Director for Metro Tunnel Project (formerly Rail Projects Victoria). The Metro Tunnel Project consists of twin 9km long tunnels and five new stations at Arden, Parkville, State Library, Town Hall and Anzac. When it opens, it will be the biggest change to Victoria’s rail network since the opening of the City Loop in 1981.

With over 20 years’ experience in project management, Ben has been involved in many significant rail projects within Victoria. He brings deep knowledge of engineering and rail construction management with a collaborative, authentic and transparent leadership approach.

Prior to leading the Metro Tunnel Project, Ben was responsible for the development of the Melbourne Airport Rail project. Before joining Rail Projects Victoria, he held senior leadership roles with John Holland on some of the most complex level crossing removals across Melbourne as part of the Level Crossing Removal Project, including level crossing removals on the Belgrave, Frankston, Craigieburn, Upfield and Mernda lines. Earlier in his career, he also spent time in the engineering consultancy sector, with a focus on the design of road and rail projects.

Presentation: Metro Tunnel’s “one team” approach to managing risk
Joshua Watkin
Former Executive Director and Head of Capital Project Delivery, Sydney Metro

Joshua has been a senior Executive with Sydney Metro, Australia’s largest public transport infrastructure program, for the past 10 years. His Executive roles have included Head of Project Delivery & Technical Services, which included responsibility for all four Metro megaprojects during the final delivery & commissioning of City-section, and the planning & commencement of the brownfield conversion of Southwest. Prior to this, Joshua led the Capital Portfolio Strategy & Assurance team, and the Program Management Office – a team of over 320 cost, schedule, risk, and digital engineering resources across all Metro projects.

Joshua retired from the Royal Australian Navy in 2015, following service in a range of national and international headquarters strategy and planning leadership roles. He holds postgraduate degrees in Theology, International Relations, and Public Administration, and is a Graduate of the Australian Institute of Company Directors.

 

Invited speakers

Asif Bhangor
Director – Power Solutions, Business Development, GS Engineering and Construction Australia and Convenor, CIGRE OHL Australian Panel

With more than 29 years in the power and energy industry Asif has led the delivery of large transmission projects including detailed design up to 500kV. He has direct experience in delivery models such as D&C, EPC and Owners Engineer.

Asif has led international working groups on power network ‘resilience’ to address challenges in overhead line design, operations and maintenance and wider asset management strategies under extreme weather events for new and ageing assets to improve safety and reliability. Asif has authored transmission line specifications, feasibility studies/tender designs, involved in supply chain management including steel manufacturers and factory acceptance testing across the Globe. 

Asif is a coach and mentor of the next generation of transmission line engineers, including university students, with his involvement with RMIT in 2022. 

Asif is the Chair for the Australian Overhead Lines Panel with the Council of Large Electric Systems (CIGRE, Australia).

Presentation: Risk management of overhead line networks: A model for identification, evaluation and mitigation of operational risks under extreme events
Nicolette Botha
Head of Climate Resilience and Sustainability APAC, Zurich Resilience Solutions

As the Head of the APAC Climate Resilience and Sustainability Team, Nicolette assists customers both nationally and globally. Her role involves helping businesses understand the physical impacts of climate change and extreme weather events. 

Nicolette provides guidance on climate adaptation and resilience measures to protect businesses, people, processes and infrastructure.

Presentation: Climate resilience in infrastructure
Anne Gibbs FIEAust CPEng EngExec NER
CEO, Asset Management Council

Dr Anne Gibbs is an executive engineering management professional with a strong focus on infrastructure management to enhance community quality of life. Anne has extensive international experience, having worked with a diverse range of communities in both developing and developed countries. Her projects have spanned aging water and waste assets, transport and social infrastructure across nations like the UK, Denmark and Russia. 

Anne has also managed the transition of a water authority in Argentina, handled municipal engineering for both remote and urban communities across Australia and undertaken humanitarian engineering assignments in Tanzanian refugee camps, as a responder to an Indonesian earthquake, and for capacity building in East Timor municipalities. Additionally, Anne provided her expertise as a Disaster Resilient Infrastructure Project Expert to the UN CDRI Secretariat. 

Anne holds a Bachelor of Civil Engineering, a Graduate Diploma in Municipal Engineering and Management, a Masters in Business Administration and a Doctorate in Business Administration.

Presentation: Turning risk into opportunities for resilient infrastructure using asset management
Andrew Harris
Executive Advisor – Critical Infrastructure and National Security, GHD

Andrew leads GHD Advisory’s practice in critical infrastructure and national security. He delivers strategic technical policy advice, business case and critical infrastructure security advice projects requiring complex engagement across multiple levels of government, utilities and with the private sector. 

His experience extends across vulnerability assessments of the energy and water sectors, business cases and advice on specialist federal government infrastructure, diplomatic property and secure buildings, the development of sovereign capability, supply chain resilience, maritime security and the security of critical infrastructure.
